item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire) (Icon Sportswire via AP Images) AP Raiola avoided throwing anyone under the bus but acknowledged what the question implied. Passing games are built on timing. If the quarterback can’t fully trust the receivers running the routes, synergy suffers and efficiency wanes. That’s less a knock on the receivers than an acknowledgment that it’s easier to develop a connection with a team’s more polished top receivers than with those thrust into action by circumstance. At times, running back Dierre Hill Jr. played wide receiver alongside freshmen Hudson Lewis and Gatlin Bair. Neither had played much until injuries hit the group. Lanning said Stewart would return. McClellan is out indefinitely. 5. The failed gadget play Much has been made about the failed gadget play in the third quarter. Many have blamed Mehringer for the play-call and the negative result hurting momentum. Let’s examine. Oregon trailed 14-10, forced an Illinois punt and took over at the Ducks’ 9-yard line. Five plays later, Oregon moved the ball to its 47. That’s when the gadget play came out. Oregon lined up with four offensive linemen to the far left, with wide receiver Dakorien Moore behind the linemen. Three Illinois defenders lined up on that side with a fourth closer to the box. Raiola checked to a run play and handed the ball to Moore on a jet sweep to the right, where the Ducks were outnumbered. The poorly-blocked play resulted in a one-yard loss. A couple of plays later, Oregon punted. After the game, Lanning was asked whether the failed play hurt the team at that moment. “Yeah, it’s a great question,” he said. “It certainly wasn’t successful. There’s a pause in operation there, right?” Yes, but who is at fault for the failed play? Is it Raiola for reading it wrong and not passing to Moore? Is it Mehringer for calling the play? Or is it Lanning for allowing the play to happen? For that play to be called, it must be accepted by Lanning, practiced, reviewed on film and further stamped by Lanning to appear on the play sheet. Then, when Mehringer calls it, Lanning must let it go through. He can hear every play call through the coaches’ headsets. If Lanning didn’t like the play, he could have vetoed it. He did not. The concept is not much different from when Lanning chooses to go for two after touchdowns. If Oregon gets the favorable look it wants, it takes the shot. That’s what happened with the gadget play. But Oregon made the wrong choice and the play failed. Regardless of the process, had Lanning not liked the play, he could have stopped it from being called. 6. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) Getty Images Still, too many drives started well before getting stuffed, putting more pressure on Raiola, who couldn’t consistently deliver. item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. RELATED: Suns vs. Blazers predictions, odds and best bets: Dame is home, and the model likes Portland on opening night Let’s catch you up. What does the starting lineup look like? The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. What about the rotation? Micah Nori , the Blazers’ first-year head coach, said he plans on using a 10-man rotation to start the season, which will allow the Blazers to capitalize on their depth and versatility. In addition to the starters, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Sidy Cissoko, Robert Williams III and Vit Krejci are expected to open the season in the rotation. The group could change depending on matchups and Williams’ availability — he did not play in back-to-backs last season — and it’s likely that Micah Potter, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen will occasionally see spot duty, as well. Wait … the Blazers have a new coach? The Blazers stabilized their turbulent coaching situation in June, hiring longtime NBA assistant Nori to replace interim coach Tiago Splitter . Nori, who interviewed for head coaching jobs seven times before finally landing his first chance, is entering his 29th season in the league and is universally revered in NBA circles for his positive approach, ability to connect with players and sharp basketball mind. Early indications have been encouraging, as the Blazers players seem to love him and the front office works well with him. The Blazers’ coaching position had been embroiled in controversy, of course, as former coach Chauncey Billups — who was placed on indefinite leave by the NBA — is facing federal felony charges related to money laundering and wire fraud conspiracy for his alleged involvement in a rigged underground poker game. What style will the Blazers play? In a stark contrast to recent seasons, the Blazers are constructed around their offense rather than their defense. The roster is unbalanced, featuring five dynamic ball-handlers and playmakers (Lillard, Morant, Avdija, Holiday and Henderson), a solid center combination (Clingan and Williams) and little wing depth. As a result, the team is expected to play fast and free under Nori, bringing lots of speed, passing, cutting and flow. Nori said he hopes to rotate his players liberally in shorter shifts during games — perhaps as short as three minutes — which will enable them to play with maximum effort before giving way to teammates. The interior defense is strong with Clingan and Williams patrolling the middle, Camara remains one of the NBA’s best and most versatile defenders and Cissoko will be asked to guard one-through-five. Holiday is still capable of locking down opposing guards and Avdija has pledged to be more of a two-way threat now that he doesn’t have to serve as the team’s primary ball-handler. But the backcourt combination of Morant and Lillard, while lethal on offense, is not imposing on defense and relatively small (both stand 6-foot-2). What are the Blazers’ expectations? Portland defied pundits last season, winning 10 of its last 14 regular season games to secure a spot in the play-in tournament, where it beat the Suns in Phoenix to earn the seventh seed in the Western Conference. The San Antonio Spurs dismissed the Blazers with a gentleman’s sweep in the playoffs , but the strong run — combined with the additions of Lillard and Morant — has raised expectations in Portland. How much? Camara said in training camp that the Blazers’ goal is to win 50 or more games and secure home-court advantage in the postseason. It won’t be easy. The league is as deep and talented as ever, and new rules surrounding the lottery should discourage teams from tanking, meaning most of the league will be chasing wins instead of lottery ping-pong balls late into the season. It seemed like a third of the league had given up last year by the All-Star break. Six of the first eight games — and 12 of the first 17 — will come on the road and include a slew of playoff contenders, including the Spurs, Oklahoma City Thunder (twice), Minnesota Timberwolves (twice), New York Knicks, Philadelphia 76ers, Denver Nuggets and Los Angeles Lakers (twice). But what about Dame? The most uplifting part of opening night figures to be the return of Lillard, the franchise icon who is back after spending two seasons in Milwaukee and one season on the injured list. The nine-time All-Star and franchise leader has not played in an NBA regular-season or playoff game since April 27, 2025, when he suffered a torn left Achilles tendon. Lillard joked earlier this week that he’s “not an old man,” but also acknowledged that he isn’t likely to play upward of 38 minutes a game like he used to and may even take a night off here and there for rest, most likely on a random back-to-back. His addition not only should help cover up two of the Blazers’ biggest weaknesses last season — three-point shooting and shooting in the clutch — but also inspire a thirsty fan base, which has rarely loved a player more. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. They’re confident they can challenge any defense vertically. “The underneath throws are going to be there,” Hampton said. “We got the best OC in the country; we’re going to be able to go deep if we want to.” Latest Beavers news Oregon State QB Braden Atkinson going through further testing of hand injury before Boise State game Oregon State basketball lands 3-star center for 2027 class Oregon State wome

item.title: Braves sign former Dodgers relief pitcher Evan Phillips to contract
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers relief pitcher Evan Phillips celebrates after San Diego Padres' Wil Myers hit into a double play to end the top of the sixth inning in Game 1 of a baseball NL Division Series Tuesday, Oct. 11, 2022, in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Marcio Jose Sanchez) The Atlanta Braves made their first move of Major League Baseball’s Winter Meetings on Thursday morning by adding a relief pitcher. The team signed reliever Evan Phillips to a 3-year, $35 million contract, adding him to what could be one of baseball’s best bullpens. [DOWNLOAD: Free WSB-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ] The 32-year-old Phillips has been with Dodgers for the past 5 seasons. His 2026 season didn’t start until July after he recovered from Tommy John surgery in June of 2025. Phillips finished 2026 with a 3-2 record, a 3.46 ERA and 33 strikeouts. He pitched 5 times for the Dodgers during the playoffs and did not give up a single run. TRENDING STORIES: SEC Week 11: No. 1 Georgia hosts No. 22 Missouri while No. 8 Texas travels to No. 24 LSU 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup: US joint bid lists Atlanta as host city Georgia Bulldogs move to the top of the College Football Playoff rankings Phillips, who hails from Clayton, NC, was originally drafted by the Braves in the 17th round of the 2015 draft. He made it to Atlanta during the 2018 season, pitching in 4 games before being traded to Baltimore. He pitched for Tampa Bay in 2021 before landing with the Dodgers. [SIGN UP: WSB-TV Daily Headlines Newsletter ] Phillips will team up with Robert Suarez, Dylan Lee and possibly Didier Fuentes to make a strong back end of the bullpen. Closer Raisel Iglesias is a free agent and it is not clear yet if he will return for another season.

item.title: After World Cup experience, Leo Nannetti shares lessons with Brazil U20s
item.description: After World Cup experience, Leo Nannetti shares lessons with Brazil U20s Brazil’s youth national teams are the natural pathway to the senior side. Goalkeeper Leo Nannetti, however, landed a golden ticket and got a “sneak peek” at life with the Seleção during the 2026 World Cup, when he was invited to join the squad and had the privilege of training alongside his idols. Now he is putting that experience to work with the U-20s and sharing what he learned with his teammates. Nannetti’s first opportunity with Brazil came with the U-17 national team in 2024, when he played in the Cascais Luso Cup. In 2025, however, he skipped a step: he joined the senior squad for training at Granja Comary ahead of World Cup qualifiers against Chile and Bolivia. In 2026, the invitation was like a VIP pass: he attended the World Cup and trained alongside Alisson, Ederson and Weverton under Taffarel’s guidance, experiencing the tournament atmosphere firsthand. Leo Nannetti: U-17 call-ups and invitations to train with the senior national team already on his résumé, and now looking forward to a tournament with the U-20s Credits: Joilson Marconne / CBF “I never imagined I would be experiencing a World Cup atmosphere at 18. It added so much to my career and my personal life. I was alongside my idols, watching how they conduct themselves, how they train and how they prepare for each game. I’ll carry that experience with me for the rest of my life,” he said. Naturally, these experiences spark curiosity among his teammates, although most already play for their clubs’ senior teams. Nannetti shares what he can and draws on the experience he has gained throughout his career to keep improving with Brazil’s U-20s. The goalkeeper has been working hard in training in Belém ahead of two friendlies against Peru Credits: Joilson Marconne / CBF “A lot of them ask what it was like, and I always try to answer as naturally as possible. The technical and mental demands change a lot from one national team to the next. The U-17s are more about development, the U-20s are very competitive, and the senior team—well, that goes without saying, doesn’t it? The pressure they carry, representing an entire nation,” he said. The goalkeeper considers one thing essential: keeping each of these experiences in perspective so he can continue developing. “I always try to keep my feet on the ground. If I’m here today, I have God, coach Paulo Victor and the coaching staff to thank for believing in my work. And I have to remember that being called up now doesn’t mean I’ll be at the South American Championship. It’s an important step, but I give my best in every training session to try to secure my place in the squad,” he concluded. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: NHL rumors: Insider floats Jason Robertson-Nikita Kucherov blockbuster trade
item.description: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images NHL rumors: Insider floats Jason Robertson-Nikita Kucherov blockbuster trade appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Neither Nikita Kucherov nor Jason Robertson is under contract beyond the 2026-27 season. With Kucherov having requested a trade and the Dallas Stars expected to revisit extension talks with Robertson in December, Daily Faceoff’s Matt Larkin floated a hypothetical blockbuster : the Tampa Bay Lightning and Stars swapping their star forwards one for one. “It’s difficult to imagine (Robertson) and the Stars getting in bed together long-term after such contentious negotiations,” Larkin wrote in his latest NHL Trade Board. “But they need him this season; it only makes sense to trade him if it’s in a hockey deal that helps them now. “How about Kucherov, one for one?” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Lightning general manager Julien BriseBois has said he doesn’t intend to trade Kucherov, but keeping him without an extension risks losing him for nothing next summer. Kucherov has been on a tear since his trade request, amassing 11 points in six games. He’s certainly not quiet quitting on the team where he won two Stanley Cups, but his future in Tampa remains in doubt. “As much as Kucherov and his camp might feel content to play out the season in Tampa, it remains to be seen if it will make things uncomfortable in the room, and it won’t stop suitors from coming forward with offers,” Larkin added. “That’s why Kucherov lands in tier 1 of this list. It’s tough to imagine this saga dragging all the way to July 1, even if his camp is fine with that happening.” Kucherov continues to be one of the NHL’s best players, now at 26 points in 18 games, while Robertson is off to another great start for the Stars, with nine goals and 19 points of his own in 17 games. Robertson’s name has been swirling in trade rumors for over a year. He reportedly turned down an eight-year offer worth about $15 million annually from the Seattle Kraken in a proposed sign-and-trade. He ended up inking a one-year, $12 million pact with Dallas to avoid arbitration, but his future remains up in the air. Both Dallas and Tampa Bay remain Stanley Cup contenders, so any deal would have to help them win now. A one-for-one swap seems unlikely, but crazier things have happened in the NHL. item.title: NFL analyst picks Bears’ Caleb Williams over NFC North rivals for playoff run
item.description: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has earned another vote of confidence ahead of the next NFL playoff race. ESPN analyst Evan Cohen picked Williams over his NFC North rivals when asked which quarterback he trusted most in a postseason situation. Speaking on ESPN’s First Take, Shae Cornette asked Cohen which division quarterback he would trust in a playoff game. Cohen chose Williams despite acknowledging the experience and recent form of his competition. “I’m going to answer it. The answer is Caleb Williams,” Cohen said. “Even though Jared Goff is the one who’s been there and done that.” MORE: Giants’ J.J. item.title: ‘I Still Talk to Him’: Aaron Rodgers Looks Forward to Reuniting with Mike Tomlin on Sunday Night
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike Tomlin after the Steelers' 34-32 win over the New York Jets on Sept. 7, 2025. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers has tuned in to watch Mike Tomlin on NBC’s Football Night in America this season. He thinks his former head coach is a natural as an analyst. “I’m not surprised in the least,” Rodgers said of Tomlin turning heads in his new role. “He is absolutely killing it on TV the few times I’ve seen him. Nobody can talk football better than Mike T, so it is an absolute match made in heaven. Him being on TV and doing what he does. And I don’t know if he still wants to coach at some point, but he’s doing a hell of a job.” Tomlin will see his former team up close and in person for the first time on Sunday night since resigning in January. “I look forward to it because of the relationships, but you know me, I’m capable of compartmentalizing, and getting hyper-focused on the job,” Tomlin said on a conference call with NBC Sports on Wednesday. “But it certainly will be fun to see some guys I got relationships with and there’ll certainly be a lot of those. But they have a job to do, I have a job to do, and so I’m sure everyone’s going to be focused on the task at hand.” Rodgers still keeps in touch with Tomlin. “I still talk to him,” Rodgers said. “I love Mike T, and I have so much appreciation for him bringing me here last year and the amount of fun that we had together. The closeness of the bond that we formed. So it’ll be good to see him.” “I’m having a lot of fun,” Tomlin said. “Haven’t given one iota of thought about coaching. I’m sure that some of that’s going to come up in the not-too-distant future. But I’ll cross that bridge when I come to it. Really haven’t thought a lot about it. Really excited about my new role and working to get better each and every week.” Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy has never seen Tomlin smile more than he is right now. “I’m really happy for Mike. I’m trying not to laugh because I’ve never seen him smile so much. I’m told he’s very happy. He’s doing a great job. So I definitely hope to run into him there in Cincinnati,” McCarthy said. Alan Saunders provided reporting from Pittsburgh. item.description: Harry Kane has broken Peter Shilton ’s appearance record for the England men’s team after playing against Croatia in the Nations League at Wembley this evening. It is the 33-year-old’s first game for his country since winning the Ballon d’Or last month and will be his record 126th England cap, meaning he surpasses Shilton atop the list. Harry Kane broke the England appearance record (PA) The legendary goalkeeper presented Kane – who has also scored a record 91 goals for the Three Lions – with a special golden crest ahead of the match at Wembley to celebrate the milestone. During the short ceremony ahead of kick-off, Kane was given a replica of the ball that Englishmen brought to Croatia in 1880 to start their love affair with football. That was presented by Croatia captain Luka Modric. Prince William also presented Kane with a framed England shirt with ‘Kane 126’ on the back before the English trio posed for photos. item.description: Atlanta Braves pitcher Evan Phillips The Atlanta Braves have made the first big splash in free agency by signing former Los Angeles Dodgers reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal. The Braves announced in a press release that Phillips will make $11 million in 2027 and 2028, and $13 million in 2029. He will also donate 1% of his salary to the Atlanta Braves Foundation. The Braves originally drafted Phillips in the 2015 MLB Draft, and he made his MLB debut with them in 2018. item.title: Sophie Cunningham names the LA Lakers player she should be compared to instead of Luka Doncic
item.description: Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images WNBA star Sophie Cunningham instantly distanced herself from a statistical comparison to Luka Doncic, and pointed the conversation in another direction. Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham discussed the Los Angeles Lakers on the latest episode of the No Hesitation podcast. Luka Doncic is averaging a stunning 38.6 ppg this season for the Western Conference leaders, putting himself in the MVP conversation. To point out just how prolific Doncic’s scoring streak is, podcast host Drew Hanlen pointed out that he is attempting almost as many shots this season as Sophie Cunningham did the entire WNBA season, and has already overtaken her for free-throws. He said: “Through his first nine games, he has attempted 221 shots. Last season in 43 games, you attempted 226 shots, so he is five behind you this season…. The second thing is, Luka has attempted 102 free throws already after nine games, and last season you attempted 74.” Sophie Cunningham asks for fairer comparison Sophie Cunningham pointed out that Luka Doncic makes a huge amount more money than she does. And instead, she asked to be compared to another Los Angeles Lakers players who she shares a more similar level of production with. She said: “And I also think you’re missing a big one: he also makes $50 million a year. I make $700,000 on my WNBA check. “You should compare me more to Quentin Grimes, we average around eight to 10 points, I think that’s it. My three-point shooting is actually better than the both of them. So if we’re going to compare, let’s compare.” It should be pointed out that Quentin Grimes is coming off the bench this season for the Lakers. His best season averaged was in 2024-25 where he posted 14.6ppg split across his spells with the Dallas Mavericks and Philadelphia 76ers. His 28-game spell exclusively with the Sixers saw him post 21.9 ppg. Sophie Cunningham’s best scoring WNBA regular season was in 2022 with the Phoenix Mercury, where she averaged 12.6 points per game. Grimes is making $13.9m with the Lakers this season as part of a four-year $60m deal signed in the offseason.

item.description: It’s been a wild season of college football and that has a lot to do with the Big Ten . Through 10 weeks, it would’ve been hard to imagine Ohio State, Michigan , and Penn State not having much of a shot at winning the Big Ten. The Buckeyes are technically still alive, but Ohio State would need a lot to go its way to win the conference. Right now, UCLA remains unbeaten and Indiana is in second with one loss. The Hoosiers have looked mortal in recent weeks, but the playoff committee might’ve made the mistake by dropping Indiana on its bye week — Curt Cignetti has found his bulletin board material. The Hoosiers will host USC, which is the big game of the week. Oregon is still fully alive , despite having three total losses. item.title: 'College GameDay' Week 11 location is a curious choice
item.description: ESPN's "College GameDay" will be having a change of pace for its Week 11 show. The GameDay crew is headed to the Pac-12 for a showdown between the No. 24 Boise State Broncos and the Oregon State Beavers . GameDay has not attended a Pac-12 game since 2023. The revamped conference is hoping to land a bid as the highest-ranked non-Power Four team in the College Football Playoff. Currently, Boise State is projected to land that spot. Based on the current rankings, Boise State would be the No. 12 seed in the playoff. GameDay has not attended Boise, Idaho, since the Broncos hosted Oregon State back in 2010 . GameDay picked the Oregon State at Boise State game over other top Nov. 14 matchups including Missouri at Georgia , Wake Forest at SMU, USC at Indiana, Michigan at Oregon, Texas at LSU, Utah at Arizona and Texas Tech at Oklahoma State. Boise State's top competition to land the non-Power Four playoff bid includes New Mexico, North Texas and Liberty. The Boise State game will be GameDay's first trip to a non-Power Four destination since attending James Madison's campus in 2023. "Get ready Boise we're coming to your city! GameDay announced via social media. "We're heading west for a Pac-12 showdown that could have CFP implications between Oregon State and Boise State." The Georgia-Missouri is GameDay's last legitimate chance to come to Athens during the regular season. We doubt GameDay would come to Georgia for the Georgia Tech game on rivalry week since Georgia Tech has had an awful season. GameDay has not come to Athens since the Ole Miss game in Oct. 2025. The last year where GameDay did not come to Athens was in 2018. item.title: FIFA fails to stop UEFA disclosure order over World Cup investor plan
item.description: FILE PHOTO - FIFA's logo is seen at FIFA headquarters ahead of the draw ceremony for the 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Zurich. (is associated with: «FIFA fails to stop UEFA disclosure order over World Cup investor plan») Christian Charisius/dpa A New York court has thrown out world football governing body FIFA's application to stop European football ruling body UEFA’s disclosure order against Thrive Capital and JP Morgan surrounding the doomed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal. FIFA president Gianni Infantino had sought to set up FFE to run the commercial interests of the World Cup and its other competitions, with private investors holding a minority stake, although the plan was abandoned in August after being rejected by three continental confederations. UEFA initially threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions, and Europe’s governing body last month demanded answers to a series of questions about FFE and a range of other concerns about Infantino’s presidency. The letter posed questions around the decision to award exclusivity to Thrive Capital to lead the FFE private investor group. Thrive was founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law JP Morgan was also confirmed by FIFA to be working alongside it on the FFE plan, having also been involved as financial backers for the doomed European Super League project in 2021. Thursday’s ruling in Manhattan means FIFA’s motion to intervene has been denied, but it is understood there needs to be another court decision to grant the disclosure of documents. Judge Jeannette Vargas wrote: “The court has already decided that the US FIFA parties have no direct, substantial and legally protectable interest in the subject matter of this application." “In light of this determination, the court exercises its discretion to decline leave to intervene,” Vargas added. The Press Association has contacted FIFA and UEFA for comment.

item.description: Bryson DeChambeau at Sugarloaf. Bryson DeChambeau / YT This week, Rory McIlroy was asked a version of a question that’s been bouncing around the golf world for months? What’s Bryson DeChambeau going to do next? Which is why, as LIV’s bankruptcy rolled on and DeChambeau’s ex-coworkers released statements about their futures, DeChambeau remained quiet, before ending up somewhere nobody expected: Western Maine. It’s 34 miles from the Canadian border. It’s 50 miles to the end of the Appalachian Trail. It’s two-and-a-half hours to Portland; Bangor is slightly closer, but offers fewer flights. “It’s remote,” Park says. “But also close enough to the real world that if you need a taste, you can get back to it real quick.” Sugarloaf doesn’t often get celebrity guests. item.title: Ohio State’s only realistic playoff path runs through Indianapolis
item.description: Ohio State has never been ranked this low by the College Football Playoff committee. The Buckeyes fell from No. 12 to No. 20 in Tuesday’s second CFP rankings after losing to Oregon, the lowest ranking Ohio State has ever received since the committee started releasing rankings in 2014. It’s also the Buckeyes’ lowest spot in the AP and Coaches polls since 2014, the week after the home loss to Virginia Tech. So where does that leave Ohio State’s playoff hopes? I’ll be honest. I don’t think the Buckeyes are making the playoff this year. Their chances are a long shot, but there is one path, and it’s actually a little more realistic than some people might think. Why 9-3 probably isn’t enough The most obvious path is winning out. Ohio State has Northwestern, at Nebraska and Michigan left. Win all three, and the Buckeyes finish 9-3. The problem is that 9-3 doesn’t do much for this resume. None of Ohio State’s remaining opponents are ranked in the CFP top 25, so there’s no chance for a big win to impress the committee. The Buckeyes would still be sitting behind a long list of two loss teams, and their three losses, at Texas, at USC and at home against Oregon, came against teams ranked ahead of them. Look at the teams between Ohio State and the edge of the 12-team field. Kentucky, Texas Tech, Wake Forest, Houston, Iowa, Oregon, South Carolina, USC and Ole Miss. Most of them have fewer losses, and two of them beat Ohio State. Even if several of those teams lose, the Buckeyes would need a ton of chaos to climb from No. 20 into an at-large spot without a quality win left on the schedule. ESPN’s Football Power Index is more optimistic, giving Ohio State a 42.6% chance to make the playoff. I don’t buy it though. Unless something crazy happens, a 9-3 Ohio State is probably gonna be watching the playoff from home. The Big Ten title game is the only real path That’s why I think Ohio State’s best path, and honestly their only one, is to get to the Big Ten Championship Game and win it. Right now, the Big Ten standings don’t look great. UCLA is 9-0 and 6-0 in conference play, Indiana is 8-1 and 5-1, while USC and Oregon are both 4-2, just like Ohio State. The Buckeyes are also behind in the tiebreakers against USC and Oregon, since they lost to both. But this season has been anything but predictable, and things could get crazy. Here’s what Ohio State would need to make the Conference Championship Game: Win out — That gets the Buckeyes to 7-2 in conference play. Indiana loses at least once more — Ohio State beat Indiana in Bloomington, so if the Hoosiers fall to 7-2 in the Big Ten, the Buckeyes would own the head-to-head tiebreaker in a two-way tie. USC and Oregon both lose at least once more — Since both beat Ohio State, the Buckeyes would need to finish ahead of them outright. USC and Indiana play each other this week as well, so at least one of these three things will happen. UCLA wins out, or stumbles too — If UCLA keeps winning, they take one spot in Indianapolis

item.title: Pierre Sage’s failure to fix defensive flaws leaves Crystal Palace seeking new solution
item.description: A losing run, set-piece struggles and a call for help led Steve Parish to cut ties with the manager after five months The moment that summed up Crystal Palace’s season under Pierre Sage came five minutes before half-time at Selhurst Park on Sunday. After Palace had gone close to taking the lead on numerous occasions against Liverpool, the Frenchman must have feared the worst when Alexis Mac Allister headed in from a soft free-kick conceded by Jefferson Lerma. The TV cameras immediately panned to Steve Parish in the stands. After the Palace chair removed his hands from in front of his eyes, his expression said everything you needed to know. The only surprise was that Sage had to wait until Thursday before his inevitable fate was confirmed . Not since the start of the 2017-18 season, after Frank de Boer was appointed as Palace’s first permanent foreign manager and sacked after five matches, have the club found themselves bottom. In their record 14th consecutive season in the top flight, and with preliminary work having started on building a new £200m main stand despite major doubts over funding, Palace cannot afford to be relegated. item.title: Football Daily | ‘Where the hell is Roy Keane!’ Fifty shades of great football debate
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Forget about Michael Carrick. Don’t dwell on Women’s Bigger Cup. Fret not about Pierre Sage. No, the big football story of the day is Big Website’s Ultimate 1-50 , a rundown of the male footballers best associated with each squad number. It’s lighthearted reading designed to entertain, maybe even inform, and perhaps spark a few memories and a touch of debate. Or, if you prefer, a rage-bait waste of time that shames the internet. Where the hell is Roy Keane! How dare you leave out Bobby Moore! And Pelé? A list without Pelé? I don’t want to live in a world where there are lists without Pelé. Such is the world these days, though surely a certain amount of respect is due to an exercise that shuns Lionel Messi and Zinedine Zidane but can welcome in Salvatore Sirigu and Mateusz Klich. item.title: From W-M to the No 10, shirt numbers tell a story of football’s tactical evolution
item.description: In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, as well as the attributes a player was supposed to demonstrate Ultimate 1-50: check out our complete list of players Numbers have a fascination. The No 10 is revered almost everywhere, but perhaps most especially in Argentina, where it denotes the playmaker, the enganche , the quasi-mythical figure who links the front and back of the team. Liverpool and Manchester United have reasons to celebrate their No 7. Ajax retired No 14 for Johan Cruyff, Milan their No 3 and No 6 for Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi respectively and Birmingham their 22 for Jude Bellingham as gestures of respect for their abilities. Other numbers have been retired to mark premature deaths: the No 20 at Liverpool for Diogo Jota, the No 23 at Manchester City for Marc-Vivian Foé, the 21 at Espanyol for Daniel Jarque. But numbers are not just about individuals. In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, and the expectations of particular numbers in particular cultures, as well as the attributes a player in that shirt was supposed to demonstrate, themselves tell a story of tactical evolution. Precisely 13,266 games have been played since the inception of the Premier League, and 19 of those matches have finished 4-4 (0.1%), a rarity in a division dominated by the mighty 1-0 (17.6%). It was about time we got one, though. The months of August and September, when teams are still fighting to define their top-flight seasons and fitness and motivation tend to be at their peak, have never seen a single 4-4 draw. As motivation decreases the chances of stupid scorelines increase, and that’s where the 4-4 creeps in. There’s a certain on-the-beachness inherent in the score, and it is no coincidence that it has occurred more in the second half of April, as thoughts drift to the close season and the ineffable pointlessness of a lot of late-campaign football becomes unavoidable, than in the entirety of any other month. Nearly 100 years ago pitch was placed in a funnel and kept at room temperature. It moves incredibly slowly at a rate of approximately one atom per second (slower than the continental drift), and only nine drips have ever been recorded , though never witnessed. item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
